name: ESCAPADE
payload: Two spacecraft, Blue and Gold: 209 kg dry, 535 kg fuelled each
delta_v: Not published; its own burns were a ~9-minute powered Earth-flyby (trans-Mars injection) burn and a ~11-minute Mars orbit insertion
first: Twin orbiters launched on New Glenn's second flight, which made the first successful landing of a New Glenn booster
description: ESCAPADE is NASA's pair of Mars spacecraft, Blue and Gold, built by Rocket Lab in a mission costing under $80 million. The principal investigator is Robert Lillis of UC Berkeley's Space Sciences Laboratory, and the mission is a NASA SIMPLEx mission from 2019 in the Heliophysics Division. Each spacecraft weighs 209 kg dry and 535 kg fuelled. They launched on New Glenn's second flight, NG-2, from Launch Complex 36 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on 13 November 2025 at 3:55 pm EST (20:55 UTC). The booster, GS1 "Never Tell Me the Odds", landed on the landing platform vessel Jacklyn about nine minutes after liftoff. Blue and Gold did not head straight for Mars: they looped around the Sun-Earth L2 point for about a year, then made powered Earth flybys, Blue on 7 November 2026 and Gold on 9 November. Their orbit-insertion burns at Mars come on 7 and 9 September 2027, about 11 minutes at 450 km, into a 60-hour capture orbit, with science due to start in June 2028.

events.label: LAUNCH
events.note: New Glenn NG-2 from Launch Complex 36, 13 November 2025, 3:55 pm EST (20:55 UTC).

events.label: SEPARATION
events.note: Blue and Gold separate from the upper stage about 33.5 minutes after liftoff.

events.label: EARTH FLYBY
events.note: Blue's powered flyby on 7 November 2026, after about a year around Sun-Earth L2; Gold follows on 9 November.

events.label: MARS ORBIT INSERTION
events.note: Burns of about 11 minutes at 450 km on 7 and 9 September 2027 put the twins into a 60-hour capture orbit.
